strongest_angle: Examining Nicolas Flamel's centuries-old will and historical records reveals how a medieval Parisian scribe and manuscript seller was transformed over 600 years into a legendary alchemist associated with the philosopher's stone.

key_facts.fact: For 600 years, writers, artists, and scientists have been fascinated by the myth of Nicolas and Pernelle Flamel, medieval Parisians said to have made gold with a philosopher's stone.

New research into the will of Nicolas Flamel, a medieval Parisian whose name became synonymous with alchemy, is revealing more about his extraordinary wealth and the origins of his legend at an exhibition opening at the Musée de Cluny in Paris.
15th-century records show that a real person named Nicolas Flamel lived in Paris working as a scribe and manuscript seller, before later 17th-century sources turned him into a successful alchemist.

numbers.label: Years of fascination with the myth
